To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) owners evicting tenants in the late 1930s were more likely to be younger, to have more land, and to live in municipalities where the rabassa morta was abolished, and that (ii) the number of evictions was higher in municipalities where the number of tenants was larger and in municipalities where the proportion of land under rabassa morta contract was higher, but not higher in municipalities where landowners had more land or where landowners were younger.

the rabassa morta contract was a long‐term contract with an average duration of 30 years; that the average rabassa morta tenancy was 1.6 ha; that the average number of tenants per rabassa morta owner was 2.6; that the average value of the rabassa mortas per owner was €1,000 in 1930; that the average annual rent per owner was €20 in 1930 and €25 in 1933; and
the rabassa morta contract was the main cause for the increase in evictions in 1930–4 and that this increase was not a result of the uncertainty over property rights.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not the legal uncertainty of the 1930’s led to a large‐scale substitution in the use of land and labour.
the impact of legal threats on the behaviour of the owners of land before 1936, and it finds that the margin for adjustment to the legal threat was small.
the effects of the uncertainty about property rights on the decisions taken by owners of land.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
land reform in the 1934–35 period had little impact on the structure of landownership, the organization of labour, and the distribution of land in Catalonia.

the 1930 reforms had a limited impact on the organization of land and labour, with the main effect being to accelerate a trend of land abandonment and the migration of labour to urban areas that had already begun in the 1920s.
the land reform of the 1930’s did not have a major impact on the organization of land and labour in Catalonia, but it did have a large impact on social and political relations in rural areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
landowners were not as responsive to threats to property rights as one could have predicted.
the rabassa morta contract was not a particularly important factor in determining landowner behaviour.
in the 1933–5 period the owners of land in Catalonia did not respond to the legal uncertainty by substituting sharecroppers and tenant farmers with wage labourers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the impact of legal uncertainty on the behaviour of landowners is not straightforward, and it is important to consider the long history of adjustment to shocks in order to understand the behaviour of owners in the face of legal uncertainty.
the impact of land reform is not only determined by the nature of the reform itself but also by the degree of adjustment of landowners to previous changes in agrarian organization.
land reform can be an effective way of reducing conflict if it is well‐targeted, and the threat of reform is not perceived as imminent by owners.
